texts.preamble: M/S Charminar Bottling Co.Pvt.Ltd., vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 2 September, 2024 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender Criminal Revision Case No.1430 Of 2010 Order:
texts.facts: The revision petitioner/A2 was convicted for the offence under Section 7(i) and punishable under Section 16(i) (a) (i) of A.P.Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of six months. 2. Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that the Food Inspector who was examined as PW.1 conducted inspection and inspected the premises of A1 on 21.05.2001. In the said premises carbonated water namely 'Pepsi' was found in bottles with capacity of 300 ml.. The said bottles were stocked for the purpose of selling. PW.1 then purchased some bottles and two bottles were sealed for the purpose of analysis. On the bottles it was mentioned that the liquid does not contain any added flavour and best before six months from the date of manufacture. Further, it was also mentioned as 'sweetened carbonated water'. The bottles were collected from A1 outlet 'Star Footwear'. The said samples were sent for the purpose of analysis. On 23.06.2001, report was sent to PW.1 stating that the test revealed that they do not conform of the standards of pH level that was required to be met. 3. Since the said bottles were manufactured by A2 company, sanction was sought which was given by the concerned authority on 25.07.2002 for prosecuting the accused. Thereafter, on 05.11.2002, the analysis report was sent to the accused. Thereafter, complaint was filed. 4. The trial Court held that the accused-company was responsible for manufacturing adulterated carbonated water, since it did not conform to the pH level standards that were prescribed. Sanction order for prosecution was obtained from the concerned State Food Authority on 25.07.2002 and notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, was issued on 05.11.2002. 6. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that orders may be passed on merits. 8. It is not disputed that the seizure and sampling of the bottles was done on 21.05.2001. Immediately, the next day it was sent for the purpose of analysis. Admittedly, neither PW.1 nor PW.2 has intimated the accused regarding the public analysis report reflecting non-conformity of pH levels prior to 05.11.2002. The shelf life of the samples is of 6 months and the accused was informed about the report after 1 year 4 months. The right to get the sample tested in accordance with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, by the Central Lab was denied on account of giving notice intimating about FSL report beyond shelf life of the product.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned Senior Counsel Sri D.Prakash Reddy, appearing on behalf of the accused would submit that the right to get the sample tested was denied by the Food Inspector. In fact, the bottles were seized on 21.05.2001, whereas the report regarding non-conformity of pH level was sent to the company on 05.11.2002 which is nearly after 1 year 4 months after the FSL had given report. In the said circumstances, when the shelf life of the produce was specifically mentioned as six months, the right to get the sample tested with the Central Lab was denied. For the reason of denial of the right of the sample being re-tested the conviction has to be reversed. The learned Senior Counsel relied on the following Judgments; i) Ahmed Dadabhai Advani v.
